sources.title: LROC WAC natural-colour global mosaic (CGI Moon Kit, lroc_color_poles_16k.tif)
sources.provider: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio / LROC team, Arizona State University
sources.note: Base colour. Adapted by NASA SVS (Ernie Wright, 2019) from the Hapke-normalised mosaic of >100,000 LRO Wide Angle Camera images (643/566/415 nm as R/G/B). The photographic mosaic covers 70°S–70°N; poleward of that SVS filled the map with monochrome LOLA laser-albedo data. Downsampled here from 16384×8192 in linear light.

sources.title: LOLA Gridded Data Record LDEM_64 / LDEM_16 (global elevation, 64 and 16 px/deg)
sources.provider: NASA GSFC / MIT — Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter team, PDS Geosciences Node
sources.note: Elevation in metres relative to a 1737.4 km sphere (DN × 0.5 m). Source of the height maps and of the normal maps, which are computed from true metric slopes at 1× relief.

sources.title: LOLA Gridded Data Record LDEC_64 / LDEC_16 (laser shot counts per pixel)
sources.provider: NASA GSFC / MIT — Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter team, PDS Geosciences Node
sources.note: Number of real altimeter measurements behind every elevation pixel (data through 2016-11-29). Pixels with zero counts were interpolated by the LOLA team. Basis of the altimetry score; LDEC_16 is shipped log-encoded as lola_counts.png.

sources.title: LOLA polar illumination products: LPSR_65N/S_240M (permanently shadowed regions) and AVGVISIB_65N/S_240M (average solar visibility), 2016-08 release
sources.provider: NASA GSFC LOLA team (Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211) — unsupported EXTRAS products
sources.note: Computed by the LOLA team from polar topography, 240 m/px, complete poleward of 65°. Used for the imagery score near the poles: permanently shadowed ground can never appear in sunlit photographs.

sources.title: LRO WAC Global Mosaic 100 m (303 px/deg) v02 — streamed tiles
sources.provider: NASA Solar System Treks (Moon Trek), JPL / LROC team, Arizona State University
sources.note: Monochrome 100 m/px mosaic streamed on demand for close-up views. Not baked into this site; availability depends on the NASA tile service.

confidenceMethod.altimetry: How much of the terrain shape was actually measured by LRO's laser altimeter (LOLA) rather than interpolated. From the LOLA shot-count grid LDEC_64 (shots per elevation pixel, 64 px/deg), counts are grouped into ground cells of about 474 m × 474 m (pixels are merged along longitude by 1/cos(latitude) so cells have the same ground size at every latitude). Score = 0.7 × (fraction of cells containing at least one real laser shot) + 0.3 × (1 − exp(−shots per km² / 100)), area-averaged over each pixel of a 2048×1024 map. LRO's polar orbit makes ground tracks converge at the poles, so coverage is densest there and thinnest in the gaps between tracks near the equator.
confidenceMethod.imagery: How well sunlit photography can show this place. Score = L × F × S. L = sqrt(min(1, sin(e)/sin(30°))) where e = 90° − |latitude| + 1.54° is the highest the Sun ever gets at local noon: no penalty until the noon Sun is below 30° (latitudes beyond about 61.5°), then a growing penalty for grazing light and long shadows. F = 0.75 poleward of 70° latitude (1 elsewhere) because the base colour map there is not photography: the LROC WAC colour mosaic stops at 70° and NASA SVS filled the caps with monochrome LOLA laser-albedo data. S uses the LOLA team's polar illumination maps (240 m/px) poleward of 65°, blended in between 65° and 67°: S = (1 − fraction of the pixel in permanent shadow) × min(1, fraction of time sunlit / 0.25); it is 0 in permanently shadowed craters, which have never been seen in direct sunlight, and reduced where the ground is lit less than half as often as an open plain. S = 1 at lower latitudes.
confidenceMethod.combined: Combined = 0.5 × average(altimetry, imagery) + 0.5 × minimum(altimetry, imagery): half the plain average and half the weaker of the two, so a place is pulled toward its weakest dataset (a permanently shadowed crater with perfect laser coverage scores 25, not 50). These scores are an index computed by this app from the published coverage and illumination products listed under sources; they are not an official NASA or LRO quality metric, and they describe global-map data support, not the accuracy of any single measurement.
